words.desc: A fast-paced film genre packed with fights, chases and dangerous physical feats.
A genre about daring journeys to exciting places in search of treasure or discovery.
A story in which beings from another planet arrive to conquer Earth.
The technique of making drawings or models appear to move by showing frames in sequence.
A film that portrays the true life story of a famous real person.
A hugely popular and expensive film that earns enormous amounts of money.
The money a film earns at cinemas, or the counter where admission is bought.
A brief appearance by a famous person in a film or show.
A high-speed pursuit between vehicles, often swerving through busy traffic.
A character destined by prophecy to save the world from a great evil.
A building where people watch films on a large screen.
A hinged slate snapped shut at the start of each take to sync picture and sound.
An ending that leaves the story unresolved at a moment of high suspense.
A kind of film or show made mainly to make the audience laugh.
The names of everyone who worked on a film, scrolling past at the end.
A genre following gangsters, robbers or the detectives trying to catch them.
The person who leads a film's creative vision and guides the cast and crew.
A sudden catastrophic event that causes great damage, loss and widespread chaos.
A non-fiction film that presents real events, people or places to inform viewers.
A serious genre focused on realistic characters facing emotional conflicts.
An outdoor cinema where people watch films from their parked cars.
Replacing a film's original spoken dialogue with a recording in another language.
A long, grand film on a huge scale, often about legendary or ancient events.
A sudden, violent burst of energy with a loud bang and flying debris.
A background performer who appears in crowd scenes without speaking lines.
A genre set in imaginary worlds where magic and impossible creatures exist.
An event where many new movies are screened, celebrated and judged by juries.
A moody genre of cynical private eyes, shadowy lighting and doomed criminals.
The climactic fight at the end of a story where good faces evil.
A scene that jumps to earlier events to show something from the past.
A brightly colored backdrop that is replaced with other images after filming.
The journey from childhood to adulthood and the lessons learned along the way.
A story's conclusion in which problems are solved and everyone is left satisfied.
A home believed to be occupied by restless spirits of the dead.
A carefully planned robbery, usually carried out by a team of skilled specialists.
The brave main character who faces danger to save others.
A film genre designed to frighten viewers with dread, shocks and terrifying threats.
A romantic situation where one person is torn between two admirers.
A wise, experienced guide who trains and advises a younger hero.
A fictional comedy filmed as if it were a serious factual film.
Using shades of only one color, such as black and white.
A sequence of short shots edited together to show time passing quickly.
A film or stage show in which characters regularly break into song and dance.
A scene in which characters stop the story to perform a song with choreography.
A story built around a puzzling event or secret that must be figured out.
The person who tells the story to the audience, often heard from offscreen.
A famous statuette awarded each year for outstanding achievement in film.
A work that imitates another in an exaggerated way for comic effect.
A sudden, unexpected turn in a story that changes everything the audience believed.
The first public screening of a new film, often a glamorous celebrity event.
A film or book set before an existing one, showing what happened earlier.
A ceremonial walkway where celebrities arrive and pose for photos at big events.
A new version of an older film, retold with a different cast and crew.
A long drive by car, often with friends, stopping at places along the way.
A story in which machines built to serve humans rebel and turn against them.
A lighthearted film genre about two people finding love through funny situations.
A genre of stories centered on two people falling in love.
A genre exploring imagined technology, futuristic worlds and their effects on people.
The written script for a film, including dialogue and directions for scenes.
A film or book that continues the story of an earlier one.
A battle between armed people firing guns at each other.
A loyal companion who helps the main character, often adding humor.
An early motion picture with no recorded dialogue, often accompanied by live music.
A film effect that stretches out movement so it plays far below normal speed.
The collection of music that accompanies a film, often released as an album.
Visual tricks and illusions used in films to create things that are not real.
Information that reveals important plot details before someone has watched or read it.
A series of drawn panels showing how each shot of a film will look.
A trained performer who replaces an actor during dangerous or physically demanding scenes.
Translated or transcribed text shown at the bottom of the screen during a film.
A costumed character with extraordinary powers who fights crime and protects the public.
A suspenseful genre that keeps audiences tense as danger and secrets slowly unfold.
Moving backward or forward to a different moment in history.
A short clip advertising an upcoming film, shown to build excitement before release.
A quick sequence showing a character practicing hard to improve before a big challenge.
The main wicked character in a story who works against the good side.
A film genre showing soldiers and battles during armed conflicts between nations.
A genre set on the American frontier featuring cowboys, outlaws and lawmen.
